Main Points
⏺ Circuit breakers temporarily halt trading during extreme moves

⏺ This post explains why pauses exist — and how they can hurt you

1️⃣ Why They Exist — to cool panic and let liquidity rebuild.
2️⃣ What Happens — trading pauses for minutes; order flow and liquidity vanish.
3️⃣ Leverage Risk — positions stay exposed, and price can gap through levels after the restart.
4️⃣ CEX vs DeFi — DeFi often lacks formal halts, but can have caps, limits, or feature shutdowns.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — avoid max leverage around news and respect post-halt gap risk.

Final Thoughts

A trading halt is a brake for the crowd. For leveraged positions, that brake can turn into a slingshot on restart.

📌 Why is Stacks (STX) going up? 

📣 Stacks has gained more than 100% over the past 90 days, backed by institutional Bitcoin Staking that is creating a new use for STX that could grow as more BTC enters future bonding periods. According to CoinGecko data, STX was trading around $0.38 on Oct. 6 after gaining roughly 18% over the previous week. The token had already climbed 108% in the 90 days through Sept. 27.

🌐 Those developments have given traders several Stacks specific catalysts at a time when many major altcoins have struggled to match STX’s gains. Bitcoin Staking is particularly important to the long term case because it gives institutions a way to earn BTC rewards while creating a separate use for STX. However, Bitcoin Staking alone cannot account for the entire 90 day rally on its own. Market conditions and renewed interest in the Stacks ecosystem have contributed to the price action as well. But unlike a short term price catalyst, the staking model creates a measurable link between institutional BTC participation and the amount of STX needed to support it.

➡️ The Genesis Bond has already put that relationship into practice, while Bond 2 and subsequent bonding periods will test whether it can repeat as more Bitcoin enters the program. Bitcoin Staking on Stacks allows BTC holders to earn BTC denominated rewards without changing Bitcoin’s proof of work consensus. Under Stacks’ Proof of Transfer system, miners commit BTC to compete for Stacks blocks and receive STX. The BTC committed through the process becomes the source of rewards distributed through the staking system.

SOL is one of the most heavily traded assets on Earth, racking up $2.4 Billion in global volume over the last 24 hours. Because the SOL↔️BTC pair moves constantly across dozens of global venues, it represents textbook arbitrage. Every single micro-movement is an opportunity automated bots actively want to capture.

### 📉 The Compression Curve In Action

As a pool grows and matures, its yield naturally stabilizes. You can see this live curve playing out right now across GalaSwap’s 0.3% fee tier pools:

* $26k Depth (SOL/BTC) ➡️ ~262% APR

This is our entire capacity thesis wrapped into three live data points: as liquidity depth grows, the rate cools. But notice how yields remain in the double digits even at nearly $1M in depth. Why? Because the volume is driven by external global market volatility, not by the size of our pool.

### 🚀 Where is the Ceiling?

How much liquidity can the SOL/BTC pool actually hold before compressing to ordinary DeFi rates?

The model indicates the ceiling is set by that massive $2.4B/day external market. Assuming a conservative 5% capture rate at the 0.3% fee tier, this single pool could productively absorb tens of millions of dollars in liquidity.

Today, it holds just $26k—roughly 0.1% of its implied capacity.

The Big Picture: One major trading pair, a pool turning over 9.5× daily, and a runway that is three orders of magnitude larger than its current size. Now consider that the GalaSwap grid has hundreds of pairs waiting to be built—some deeper, some hotter, and most still completely untouched.

Good morning from Galilee.

Many of you know I have been struggling with sleep deprivation. Almost every night, I wake up around 2 or 3 a.m. and struggle to fall asleep again. Sometimes I manage another hour of sleep. Other times, by 5 a.m., I simply get up.

Many send me Bible verses about the rest the Lord gives His people, and I am grateful. Yet sometimes I feel the Spirit urging me to pray and consider my next steps as a believer.

The life of faith is anything but passive. We are called to run the race, fight the good fight, and keep the faith. And we must do so with purpose:

“Therefore I run thus: not with uncertainty. Thus I fight: not as one who beats the air.”
1 Corinthians 9:26, NKJV

I believe another storm is brewing in the Middle East, one that could break before this year ends. A weakened Iranian regime may try to strike again rather than accept its decline. The concern is that preparations for an Iranian attack could prompt Israel to strike first.

Meanwhile, we are watching support for Israel erode among the younger generation of our greatest ally.

Too many Christians remain silent. Others join the bandwagon of hostility toward Israel, fueled by ignorance and biblical illiteracy.

And here I am, at home overlooking the Jezreel Valley, a battlefield of the past and the gathering place for a future battle, asking myself: Am I doing enough?

I would rather ask what more I can do than assume all is well and become complacent.

As I travel the world and meet people face to face, I hear firsthand how my books have helped them and their loved ones emerge from despair and anxiety, focus on the Word, and stand with Israel.

I know God has called me to teach. I am neither a pastor nor a preacher. I am a simple teacher who once traveled the roads of Israel, teaching busloads of tourists. Today, I do the same in larger venues and through more than a microphone.

Writing books is a passion I never knew I had. Seeing what God has shown me poured onto pages that will remain long after I am gone brings me deep peace and gratitude.

Yet even that can never replace meeting people in person around the world.

Let’s warn the world about what is coming and proclaim the hope of salvation in Messiah Yeshua.

Let’s strengthen and encourage one another as we see the Day approaching:

“And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.”
Hebrews 10:24–25, NKJV

Let’s stop attacking one another and join hands in the battle against the works of the evil one. Our enemy seeks to steal, kill, and destroy. Our Messiah gives life:

“The thief does not come except to steal, and to kill, and to destroy. I have come that they may have life, and that they may have it more abundantly.”
John 10:10, NKJV
